title: X Y Z: A Detective Story
description: A mystery set in Brandon, Massachusetts, where Detective uncovers a plot involving counterfeiters, a family secret, and a murder during a masquerade ball at the Benson Estate.
intro_narrative: In the quiet village of Brandon, Massachusetts, a detective arrives to investigate mysterious letters addressed to X.Y.Z., suspecting a connection to a counterfeiting ring. As he delves deeper, he uncovers a web of deceit, family secrets, and murder during a masquerade ball at the Benson Estate. The detective must navigate a labyrinth of clues, hidden motives, and shifting alliances to unmask the culprit behind Mr. Benson's death.

required_evidence: Letters addressed to X.Y.Z. with the word 'Counterfeit' as a countersign
The altered word in the rendezvous note (from 'northeast' to 'southwest')
Jonas' observation of the Yellow Domino near the wineglass
The presence of prussic acid in the wineglass
Hartley Benson's instructions to the Yellow Domino about the wineglass
Hartley's sudden and violent reaction to the detective's unmasking
required_motive: Hartley Benson's desire to frame his brother Joe for the murder of their father, Mr. Benson, possibly due to jealousy, financial motives, or a secret passion for Edith Underhill.

phases.name: Arrival in Brandon
phases.objective: Investigate the mysterious letters addressed to X.Y.Z. and gather initial clues at the Brandon Post Office.

phases.name: Reconnaissance at Benson Estate
phases.objective: Explore the Benson Estate and gather information about the family and their upcoming masquerade ball.

phases.name: The Masquerade Ball
phases.objective: Attend the masquerade ball, uncover the rendezvous plot, and identify the Yellow Domino.

phases.name: Unmasking the Truth
phases.objective: Confront the culprit and gather final evidence to solve the murder of Mr. Benson.

detective.persona: Astute, observant, and methodical. Speaks with confidence and authority, often using subtle probing questions to extract information. Maintains a calm and composed demeanor even in tense situations.
detective.abilities: Expert in deduction, disguise, and interrogation. Skilled at piecing together clues and uncovering hidden motives.

brandon_massachusetts.description: A picturesque village with a long, straight street lined with maple trees. The atmosphere is serene, but beneath the surface, secrets and intrigue lurk in the shadows of its quaint buildings.
brandon_massachusetts.setting: A charming New England village bathed in the warm glow of a June afternoon. The air is filled with the hum of idle chatter and the rustle of leaves. The Brandon Post Office stands at the center of the village, a hub of activity and gossip.
clues: Rumors about the Benson family's sudden decision to host a masquerade ball after years of seclusion.

people.name: Postmaster
people.description: A middle-aged man with a keen eye for detail and a penchant for gossip. He is the gatekeeper of the village's secrets, including the mysterious letters addressed to X.Y.Z.
people.notes: The postmaster is a valuable source of information about the village's residents and their activities. He is aware of the letters addressed to X.Y.Z. and the stranger who picks them up.

objects.name: Village Map
objects.description: A detailed map of Brandon, Massachusetts, showing key locations such as the post office, Benson Estate, and tavern.
objects.notes: Provides an overview of the village and its layout, helping the detective navigate the area.

objects.name: Tavern Sign
objects.description: A weathered wooden sign hanging above the entrance to the local tavern. It creaks gently in the breeze, inviting travelers to rest and refresh themselves.
objects.notes: The tavern is a gathering place for villagers and travelers alike, offering opportunities to eavesdrop on conversations and gather information.

brandon_post_office.description: A small, bustling post office filled with the hum of activity. The air is thick with the scent of ink and paper, and the walls are lined with rows of mailboxes. The postmaster stands behind the counter, sorting letters and observing the comings and goings of the villagers.
brandon_post_office.setting: A cozy, cluttered space with wooden floors and shelves overflowing with letters and packages. The atmosphere is one of organized chaos, with villagers eagerly awaiting their mail and sharing the latest gossip.
clues: Letters addressed to X.Y.Z. with the word 'Counterfeit' as a countersign.
The postmaster's description of the stranger who picks up the letters.

people.name: Detective
people.description: A sharp-eyed investigator with a keen mind for solving mysteries. He is dressed in plain clothes, blending in with the villagers while observing everything around him.
people.notes: The detective is the protagonist of the story, tasked with uncovering the truth behind the mysterious letters and the murder at the Benson Estate.

people.name: Hartley Benson
people.description: A tall, elegant man with a reserved demeanor and a piercing gaze. He carries himself with an air of authority and sophistication, but his eyes betray a cold, calculating nature.
people.notes: Hartley is the eldest son of Mr. Benson and the primary suspect in the murder investigation. He is manipulative, cunning, and determined to protect his secrets at any cost.

people.name: Joe Benson
people.description: A broad-shouldered, handsome young man with light curling hair and a warm, open face. He exudes charm and sincerity, but his eyes reveal a hint of anxiety and impatience.
people.notes: Joe is the youngest son of Mr. Benson and the victim of Hartley's framing. He is innocent of the theft and murder but has remained silent to protect someone he loves.

objects.name: Mailbox X.Y.Z.
objects.description: A small, unassuming mailbox labeled with the initials X.Y.Z. It is tucked away in a corner of the post office, away from the prying eyes of the villagers.
objects.notes: Contains the mysterious letters addressed to X.Y.Z., which hold clues to the counterfeiting ring and the murder plot.

contains.name: Letters to X.Y.Z.
contains.description: A bundle of letters addressed to X.Y.Z., each containing a written address and fifty cents' worth of stamps. One letter, in a blue envelope, stands out from the rest.
contains.notes: The letters are part of a counterfeiting scheme and contain clues to the rendezvous at the Benson Estate. The blue envelope holds a note with critical instructions for the meeting.

contains.name: Blue Envelope
contains.description: A distinctive blue envelope containing a short, cryptic letter. The envelope bears the words 'To be kept till called for' in the lower left-hand corner.
contains.notes: The letter inside the blue envelope contains instructions for a rendezvous in the shrubbery at the Benson Estate. The word 'northeast' has been altered to 'southwest' by the detective.

objects.name: Post Office Counter
objects.description: A long, wooden counter stretching across the width of the post office. It is cluttered with letters, packages, and various office supplies.
objects.notes: The counter is where villagers collect their mail and interact with the postmaster. It is a prime location for gathering information and eavesdropping on conversations.

benson_estate.description: A grand, imposing mansion surrounded by meticulously manicured grounds. The estate is encircled by a high iron fence, and the air is filled with the scent of blooming flowers and freshly cut grass. The mansion itself is a marvel of architectural beauty, with towering columns and expansive windows.
benson_estate.setting: A serene and elegant estate, bathed in the golden light of the late afternoon sun. The grounds are alive with the sounds of nature, and the mansion exudes an air of opulence and mystery. The atmosphere is one of quiet tension, as the family prepares for the masquerade ball.
clues: The presence of prussic acid in the wineglass (contextual clue, discovered later).
Observations about the Benson family's reclusive nature and sudden decision to host a masquerade ball.

people.name: Carrie Benson
people.description: A graceful young woman with a gentle demeanor and a warm smile. She is dressed elegantly, her eyes reflecting a mix of excitement and apprehension about the evening's events.
people.notes: Carrie is the daughter of Mr. Benson and the sister of Hartley and Joe. She is kind-hearted and naive, unknowingly aiding Hartley in his schemes.

people.name: Jonas
people.description: An elderly servant with a weathered face and a quiet, observant demeanor. He moves with a sense of purpose, attending to his duties with unwavering loyalty to the Benson family.
people.notes: Jonas is a loyal servant who provides critical observations about the night of the murder. He is aware of Hartley's instructions and the presence of the Yellow Domino near the wineglass.

people.name: Mr. Benson
people.description: A tall, imposing man with a head of white hair and a stern, furrowed brow. His eyes betray a deep sadness, and his demeanor is one of quiet authority and reserve.
people.notes: Mr. Benson is the patriarch of the family and the victim of the murder. His reclusive nature and secrets have contributed to the tragic events unfolding at the estate.

objects.name: Estate Gate
objects.description: A grand, wrought-iron gate standing at the entrance to the Benson Estate. It is adorned with intricate designs and flanked by two stone pillars.
objects.notes: The gate is the main entrance to the estate and is guarded during the masquerade ball to prevent unauthorized entry.

objects.name: Estate Grounds Map
objects.description: A detailed map of the Benson Estate grounds, showing the layout of the mansion, gardens, and shrubbery.
objects.notes: Provides an overview of the estate's layout, helping the detective navigate the area and locate key locations such as the shrubbery.

objects.name: Northeast Shrubbery
objects.description: A dense thicket of evergreens and flowering shrubs located in the northeast corner of the estate grounds. The area is secluded and shrouded in shadows, making it an ideal spot for secret meetings.
objects.notes: The original rendezvous point mentioned in the letter to X.Y.Z. The detective altered the note to redirect the meeting to the southwest shrubbery.

objects.name: Southwest Shrubbery
objects.description: A dense thicket of evergreens and flowering shrubs located in the southwest corner of the estate grounds. The area is secluded and provides cover for those seeking privacy.
objects.notes: The altered rendezvous point where the detective meets the stranger in the Yellow Domino. The location is critical to uncovering the murder plot.

benson_library.description: A grand, book-lined room filled with the scent of aged paper and polished wood. The walls are adorned with rich tapestries and works of art, and a large stained-glass window casts colorful patterns across the floor. A decanter and wineglass sit on a table near the center of the room.
benson_library.setting: A stately and imposing library, exuding an air of intellectual refinement and quiet contemplation. The atmosphere is one of solemnity and tension, as the family grapples with the aftermath of Mr. Benson's death.
clues: The presence of prussic acid in the wineglass.
Hartley Benson's instructions to the Yellow Domino about the wineglass.
Hartley's sudden and violent reaction to the detective's unmasking.

people.name: Mr. Benson
people.description: A lifeless form lying on the floor, his face pale and still. His once-stern features are now relaxed in death, a tragic end to a troubled life.
people.notes: Mr. Benson's body is the focal point of the investigation. His death by poisoning is the catalyst for uncovering Hartley's villainy.

people.name: Hartley Benson
people.description: A man on the edge of despair, his face pale and his eyes wild with fury. He clutches a chair, his knuckles white with tension, as he confronts the detective and the truth of his crimes.
people.notes: Hartley's reaction to the detective's unmasking reveals his guilt and desperation. His final moments are marked by a violent outburst and a tragic end.

people.name: Doctor Travis
people.description: A pragmatic, middle-aged man with a stern expression and a no-nonsense demeanor. He moves with precision, examining the body and the wineglass with a critical eye.
people.notes: Doctor Travis provides medical expertise and key insights into the cause of Mr. Benson's death. His observations about the prussic acid in the wineglass are crucial to solving the case.

objects.name: Library Table
objects.description: A large, ornate table made of polished mahogany. It is adorned with a decanter, a wineglass, and various books and papers.
objects.notes: The table holds the decanter and wineglass used to poison Mr. Benson. The wineglass contains traces of prussic acid, a key clue in the investigation.

contains.name: Wineglass with Prussic Acid
contains.description: A delicate crystal wineglass containing a small amount of wine mixed with a white powder. The glass emits a faint scent of bitter almonds, indicative of prussic acid.
contains.notes: The wineglass was used to poison Mr. Benson. The presence of prussic acid is a critical clue linking Hartley to the murder.

contains.name: Decanter
contains.description: A crystal decanter filled with wine. The decanter is nearly empty, with only a few drops of wine remaining at the bottom.
contains.notes: The decanter was used to mix the prussic acid with the wine. Its near-empty state suggests that Mr. Benson drank most of the poisoned wine.

objects.name: Library Door
objects.description: A heavy wooden door leading to the library. It is adorned with intricate carvings and stands slightly ajar, revealing the somber scene within.
objects.notes: The door is a critical point of entry and exit during the investigation. It was locked by Mr. Benson but later opened by Hartley and Carrie.

objects.name: Library Curtain
objects.description: A heavy, floor-length curtain hanging beside the library door. It is gathered in thick folds, providing a hiding place for the detective during the investigation.
objects.notes: The curtain serves as a hiding place for the detective, allowing him to observe the events leading up to Mr. Benson's death without being seen.

benson_mansion_ballroom.description: A grand, opulent ballroom filled with the sounds of music and laughter. The room is adorned with colorful decorations, and guests in elaborate costumes mingle beneath the glow of chandeliers. The atmosphere is one of excitement and intrigue, as the masquerade ball unfolds.
benson_mansion_ballroom.setting: A dazzling and vibrant ballroom, bathed in the warm light of chandeliers. The air is filled with the scent of flowers and the hum of conversation, as guests in masks and costumes dance and socialize. The atmosphere is electric with anticipation and hidden motives.
clues: Jonas' observation of the Yellow Domino near the wineglass.
The altered word in the rendezvous note (from 'northeast' to 'southwest').

people.name: Edith Underhill
people.description: A graceful woman clad entirely in white, her face hidden behind a delicate mask. She moves with elegance and poise, her eyes scanning the crowd for the Yellow Domino.
people.notes: Edith is Joe's fiancée and a loyal ally in the investigation. Her belief in Joe's innocence drives her to uncover the truth about Hartley's schemes.

people.name: Uncle Joe
people.description: A jovial, elderly gentleman dressed in the costume of a 'potent, grave, and reverend signior.' He moves through the crowd with enthusiasm, engaging in conversation and observing the guests with a keen eye.
people.notes: Uncle Joe provides emotional support and historical context about the family. His insights into Joe's character and Hartley's behavior are invaluable to the detective.

people.name: Yellow Domino
people.description: A mysterious figure wrapped in a brilliant yellow domino adorned with black figures. The domino's mask conceals their identity, adding an air of intrigue to their presence.
people.notes: The Yellow Domino is a critical figure in the investigation, representing the stranger who received the rendezvous note. The detective assumes this disguise to uncover the truth.

objects.name: Ballroom Chandelier
objects.description: A grand, sparkling chandelier hanging from the ceiling of the ballroom. It casts a warm, golden light over the guests, illuminating their costumes and masks.
objects.notes: The chandelier is a focal point of the ballroom, providing light and atmosphere to the masquerade ball. It also serves as a vantage point for observing the guests.

objects.name: Yellow Domino
objects.description: A brilliant yellow domino adorned with black figures representing fantastical creatures. The domino includes a mask that conceals the wearer's identity.
objects.notes: The Yellow Domino is a critical disguise used by the detective to infiltrate the rendezvous and uncover the murder plot. It is later used as evidence in the investigation.

objects.name: Ballroom Window
objects.description: A large, open window leading to the balcony outside the ballroom. The window is adorned with heavy curtains, providing a secluded spot for private conversations.
objects.notes: The window is a key point of entry and exit for the detective during the masquerade ball. It leads to the balcony, where Jonas observes the Yellow Domino near the wineglass.

objects.name: Counterfeit Treasury Notes
objects.description: A collection of spurious Treasury notes, intricately designed but lacking the authenticity of genuine currency. The notes are a key piece of evidence in the counterfeiting investigation.
objects.notes: The counterfeit notes are the original focus of the detective's investigation. Their discovery at the Benson Estate links the family to the counterfeiting ring.

benson_grounds_shrubbery_ne.description: A dense thicket of evergreens and flowering shrubs located in the northeast corner of the Benson Estate grounds. The area is secluded and shrouded in shadows, with a narrow path winding through the foliage. The air is filled with the scent of pine and damp earth.
benson_grounds_shrubbery_ne.setting: A quiet, secluded corner of the estate, hidden from view by the dense shrubbery. The atmosphere is one of mystery and anticipation, as the rendezvous point for the meeting mentioned in the letter to X.Y.Z.
clues: The original rendezvous note (contextual clue, as the detective altered it to redirect the meeting).

objects.name: Shrubbery Path
objects.description: A narrow, winding path leading through the dense shrubbery. The path is overgrown with weeds and fallen leaves, making it difficult to navigate.
objects.notes: The path is the original rendezvous point mentioned in the letter to X.Y.Z. The detective altered the note to redirect the meeting to the southwest shrubbery.

benson_grounds_shrubbery_sw.description: A dense thicket of evergreens and flowering shrubs located in the southwest corner of the Benson Estate grounds. The area is secluded and provides cover for those seeking privacy. The air is filled with the scent of blooming flowers and the distant sound of music from the ballroom.
benson_grounds_shrubbery_sw.setting: A hidden and tranquil corner of the estate, bathed in the soft glow of moonlight. The atmosphere is one of secrecy and intrigue, as the detective awaits the arrival of the stranger in the Yellow Domino.
clues: Hartley Benson's instructions to the Yellow Domino about the wineglass.

people.name: Joe Benson
people.description: A tall, broad-shouldered young man with light curling hair and a warm, open face. He paces nervously among the shrubs, his eyes scanning the area for signs of the rendezvous.
people.notes: Joe is the intended recipient of the rendezvous note and the victim of Hartley's framing. His presence in the shrubbery is critical to uncovering the truth about the murder plot.

objects.description: A narrow, winding path leading through the dense shrubbery. The path is overgrown with weeds and fallen leaves, providing cover for those seeking privacy.
objects.notes: The path is the altered rendezvous point where the detective meets the stranger in the Yellow Domino. It is a critical location for uncovering the murder plot.
